messages:
Sam W: Quick sync — proposing we formalize a 'debt tranching' approach for long-lived refactors. Instead of full-service extractions, we group related tech debt into tranches with clear acceptance gates and ownership handoffs. Thoughts?
Nina R: +1. Need concrete gates tho — e.g., API contract, perf budget, observability hooks.
Bryce L: Curious about migration risk. how do we avoid two-team ownership limbo?
Sam W: plan idea: tranche = coherent set of files + tests. Owner (team A) implements adaptor + compatibility shim. Tranche gate = automated contract tests, latency < Xms on p95, and feature-flagged traffic. After gate, ownership transfer to team B.
Maria K: This feels like a good way to schedule paydown. Can we make tranche size small (2–4 sprint work)? Big tranches stall.
Bryce L: Agree. Also add rollback criteria and a canary runbook. We should require perf harness before cutover.
Nina R: Example acceptance checklist I'd include:
- contract-schema.yaml validated across clients
- integration tests > 90% coverage for adapter paths
- tracing spans for new boundary
- cost delta measured on staging
- migration rollback plan documented
(we can store templates in infra repo)
Sam W: putting a concrete rule: no tranche larger than ~40 LOC churn per service owner? (joke) seriously: cap on diff and runtime surface. But we should prioritize riskier seams first.
InfraBot: Deploy check: new canary pipeline template available at https://ci.internal/redwood/canary-templates (run `./ci canary --tranche <id>`).
Maria K: Operational question — who owns the compatibility shim long-term? Keep with old owner until full cutover, right?
Sam W: yes. Owner retains shim until telemetry shows <1% fallback and no regressions for 2 weeks. Then repo transfer + remove shim.
Bryce L: How do we communicate tranche boundaries in the codebase so reviewers understand scope?
Nina R: Add a tranche header in changed files and a single tranche PR that references a central ticket. Eg: `// TRANCHE: 2024-TR-17 - adapter + contract` and include `tranche.yaml` with metadata.
Maria K: Also require a tiny dashboard widget (console) that shows tranche health (#requests, errors, fallback rate). That will help PMs and SREs.
Sam W: Action items:
- Nina: draft tranche acceptance checklist + `tranche.yaml` schema (due Tue)
- Bryce: prototype canary pipeline snippet and perf harness example (due Fri)
- Maria: dashboard widget mock + SLO thresholds (due next Wed)
- Infra: add template to CI (InfraBot acknowledged)
Bryce L: I'll start with a small tranche for the request router -> enricher boundary to test the flow.
Nina R: FYI we should tie tranche IDs to our planning board so PMs can see payoff.
Sam W: thanks — aim to run pilot tranche next sprint. Keeping scope tight and having rollback + telemetry requirements are the key takeaways. :thumbsup:
Maria K: sounds good. I'll book a 30m follow-up for deployment runbook review.
InfraBot: Noted. Canary template PR opened: https://ci.internal/redwood/pulls/3128
Sam W: perfect. If anyone has other constraints (compliance, infra tenancy) call them out in the tranche ticket. Otherwise we proceed with pilot.
